Plays a lot like Gunfire Reborn, but I would say this game is much smoother and polished. The story is not too deep and there's lore in the form of cards picked up through play. There is player progression in the form of camp upgrades, which make me feel like I'm never wasting time. I was surprised by the number of things I unlocked just by exploring and look forward to continue playing. Worked great on my deck but I had to turn down some settings from the default because the fan was going pretty hard during normal play.

Great gunplay, fun movement and good roguelite mechanics. 
My only complaint is that co-op is limited to 2 players, although the game is very clearly designed with both solo play and 2 player co-op in mind so increasing the player count would take significant effort.
This game has come a very long way since I first played early access nearly 3 years ago and now it has probably become my favorite roguelite, highly recommend it if you're into first person shooters and roguelites.

I can now feel like i can recommend this game entirely, many if not all my complaints were somewhat covered, that being said there is still SOME relevency and truth in my old review, so im keeping it within this box, (it still suffers from "oh ok, guess that's it then") once you get ahead of the curve with what seems to be two valid playstyles (hunker and bunker or run and gun) the game does become quite a bit of fun to figure out, that being said, you really have to work for your masterclass build what i mean is there is a LOT of involved rng and you just have to take the best case in every roll and be smart with your rerolling (dont spend it all right away hoping for the best things if your runner up is there). there also IS a way to remove guns out of the pool, up to 12 of them actually, and if there are more guns you dislike than like you can just double its chances of  a gun you ACTUALLY like appearing instead, its difficult to get to this point but its exceptionally worth it if you plan to explore the game as I have.

this game suffers from a fairly suffocating game-play loop, what i mean by that is on paper it sounds like a lot of fun and it is for a few runs, but after a while, you can sum up a majority of runs to "oh OK. guess that's it then." you don't feel like your improving at a noticeable rate, your unlocking things and that helps you progress easier, and in general I've never been so baffled to see my skill feel capped, and this is entirely pushing "skill issue" aside, obviously playing better rewards you, however with how somewhat limited your survival options are in this game (normally not an issue but it is noticeable in a game like this) you end up wanting more mobility options or ways to restore your scratch hp (a secondary hp bar over your main hp bar that ISNT hp, but is easily able to become your main hp, I explain it poorly here though, try the demo) now that's not to say i want the game to be easier, I fully understand why I lose a lot of runs to a random projectile (namely i don't move well enough to naturally dodge everything, meaning when i don't see something fly at me i end up getting hit)
but that's exactly why the game feels like a chore, i die in the same place every game, everything before it is S rank andd then I reach that one part i struggle with and die less than a quarter way... again. "oh OK. guess that's it then." even a form of "training" mode (or a wave survival) would do wonders for the natural process of this game, maybe select an arena like oasis or ruins and just play with a changing environment and generated enemies, that way you can get into a groove and understand the enemies better, besides that? I want more control over the rng of the game OTHER than more rerolls and more options, give me the ability to at least partially hand pick traits on a weapon, or at least let me pick a weapon of my choosing to use more often like the kunai.

Possibly the best RougeLite ive played, as well as being a VERY solid FPS game. The gameplay is robust, yet fluid, the movement is a mix of quake and titanfall, the artystyle is exteramly polished. Gameplay loop is fun, and takes time to master, no 2 runs are the same. Class diversity is prominent and well done, each robot feels unique in its playstyle and there is enough variety for a good amount of replayability. Enemy designs are unique and become second nature when you're in game, making it easy to diagnose what ones require your immediate attention during your run. 

Overall this game has been a great surprise, i picked it up on a gamble, as im mainly a multiplayer FPS player, but iver REALLY enjoyed my time with RoboQuest, Highly recommended.

One of the best games of the year.  Fantastic fps gameplay, coming from someone who doesn't much like FPS games.  It's borderlands without the flaming psychos and shoved into a roguelite formula.  Get this is you have a friend to play with or like fps on your own.  It's good on your own, it's way better with your brobot.

It's an incredible shooter, and an incredible rogue-like. I played the demo for hours and then decided to actually buy the game so i could support the developers. Every weapon is different in their own way, and each weapon has modifiers that it can have, honestly the more I play it the more i fall in love with it. The soundtrack is also incredible (Just get to The Fields and you'll know)  I'm really looking forward to Roboquest's future. From how fluid the movement feels, to how fresh the graphics look, I cannot recommend this game enough.
